# An exact unique-sector envelope from actual chord endpoints

This planar lemma bounds one sector of an arbitrary convex body using
four of its actual radial chord endpoints. It is not a general upper
bound on whole-body area: the determinant condition below is necessary
for this particular envelope to be bounded.

Let K be a planar convex body with0 in its interior. Write the six
actual intersections of its boundary with x=0, y=0 and x+y=0 as

    (A,0), (-a,0), (0,B), (0,-b),
    (rho,-rho), (-tau,tau),

where all six parameters are positive. Let

    R_3=K intersect {x<=0,y<=0},
    D_3=rho*a+tau*b-a*b.

Closed sector boundaries have area zero. If D_3>0, then

    |R_3| <= E_3,
    E_3=[ab(a*tau+b*rho)-rho*tau(a-b)^2]/(2D_3).       (1)

All coordinates and areas here are in the same canonical coordinate
system. Cyclic changes (x,y) to (y,-x-y) or (-x-y,x) have determinant1,
so the corresponding formulas need no area rescaling.

## 1. Two actual segment constraints

For (-u,-v) in R_3, u,v>=0, join this point to (rho,-rho) in K.
The segment's crossing with x=0 has y-coordinate

    -rho(u+v)/(rho+u).

It cannot be below the actual negative y intercept -b. Hence

    (rho-b)u+rho*v<=rho*b.                         (2)

Join the same point to (-tau,tau). Its crossing with y=0 has
x-coordinate -tau(u+v)/(tau+v), which cannot be left of -a.
Consequently

    tau*u+(tau-a)v<=tau*a.                        (3)

These inequalities come from actual segments in the SAME convex K.
They do not assume supporting lines at the chord endpoints. Applying
them to the two actual sector endpoints (a,0),(0,b) gives

    rho(a-b)<=ab,    tau(b-a)<=ab.                 (4)

Let P denote the nonnegative-quadrant intersection of (2),(3).
The reflected sector is contained in P, and P contains the triangle
with vertices0,(a,0),(0,b), by (4).

## 2. Boundedness and the exact polygon

Suppose D_3>0. Any nonzero nonnegative recession direction (u,v)
would satisfy the homogeneous versions of (2),(3). Boundedness
can be checked without a sign-ambiguous subtraction as follows.
If rho>=b, (2) bounds v and, when rho>b,
also u; if rho=b, (3) then bounds u. The symmetric argument applies
when tau>=a. In the remaining case rho<b and tau<a, a recession
direction with u>0 would obey

    v/u <=(b-rho)/rho,
    v/u >=tau/(a-tau).

Such a direction exists only if rho*tau<=(a-tau)(b-rho),
equivalently D_3<=0. A direction with u=0 is also ruled out by (2).
Thus D_3>0 makes P bounded in every case.

The axis intercepts are exactly(a,0),(0,b). The only possible other
nonzero vertex is the intersection of the two oblique lines. Cramer's
rule gives

    P_*=(rho[ab+tau(a-b)]/D_3,
         tau[ab+rho(b-a)]/D_3).                    (5)

The numerators are nonnegative by (4). If one is zero, this point
coincides with the corresponding axis vertex, so the same polygon
description holds with a repeated vertex omitted. Both lines support
the feasible quadrant intersection, and the axis triangle is feasible;
hence the polygon is precisely

    conv{0,(a,0),P_*,(0,b)}.

Its shoelace area is (a P_*y+b P_*x)/2. Substitution and collecting
the cross terms give exactly E_3 in (1). This proves the bound.

For completeness, if D_3<=0 then necessarily rho<b and tau<a.
The interval of recession slopes just displayed is nonempty, so this
particular two-line envelope is unbounded. No finite area claim is
made in that case, even though the original K is compact.

## 3. Cyclic sectors and the cap-fraction consequence

Let v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1). The other two unique sectors
are R_1=K intersect {y<=0,x+y>=0} and
R_2=K intersect {x<=0,x+y>=0}. In the corresponding cyclic coordinates,
the four parameters (a,b,rho,tau) in (1) become respectively

    R_1: (rho,A,B,b),
    R_2: (B,tau,a,A).

Their envelope determinants are therefore

    D_1=B*rho+b*A-rho*A,
    D_2=a*B+A*tau-B*tau,
    D_3=rho*a+tau*b-a*b.                           (6)

Whenever D_i>0 its area capacity E_i is given by the corresponding
substitution in (1).

Suppose all three actual cap areas K_i=|K intersect {v_i.x>=0}|
are at most c k, with k=|K| and c<1/2. The complement of the other
two caps is R_i up to null boundaries. Inclusion-exclusion gives

    |R_i|=k-K_j-K_l+|K intersect H_j intersect H_l|
          >=(1-2c)k.

Thus every bounded sector envelope supplies the explicit upper bound

    k<=E_i/(1-2c).                                (7)

For the current critical cap fraction c=128/279, this is
k<=279 E_i/23. The result is ready to combine with ACTUAL ray lengths
and their critical chord-center restrictions. No assertion is made
here that one D_i has a required uniform positive lower bound, or
that (7) reaches a numerical OC threshold.
